trades.headline: Their second quarterback scores them nothing every week, and their flex is currently a tight end
trades.yourSurplus: Golden finished week 1 with 15.5, which is better than yesterday's read of him and makes this a slightly worse trade than it looked. He is still your WR4 behind Rice and Wilson and does not enter the lineup while both are healthy.
trades.theirHole: Team 13 roster Josh Allen and Lamar Jackson and can start one. They are also starting Travis Kelce in the RB/WR/TE flex because no third receiver clears him. Golden fixes the flex; the quarterback they give up was never going to play.
trades.yourLineup: Allen replaces Stafford, which after week 1 is the largest weekly upgrade available anywhere on this roster — Stafford scored 4.1 while Lawrence scored 25.6 on your bench.
trades.theirLineup: They keep Lamar at quarterback and put Golden in the flex over Kelce.
trades.risk: Golden's 15.5 raises his price and they may now value him correctly, which makes this harder rather than easier. Lead with their flex problem, not with your quarterback problem. And note you no longer need a quarterback urgently — Lawrence solves it for free.

candidates.note: 29.8 points, 8 of 9 for 138 and two scores, led Carolina in every receiving category. 50% rostered is an anomaly in a ten-team league. Worth having — but not worth this league's waiver priority, which never resets. He projects as a flex competing with Tuten and Lloyd, not a starter who fixes a hole. He clears Wednesday 07:00 UTC. If nobody claims him, add him free.

This row exists to stop a mistake, and it still does. Hunter shows rank 1 in the data, which reads like the best player on the wire. He is not. Jacksonville list him as a starting cornerback and backup receiver; he played four offensive snaps in week 1 on one designed touch. His ownership fell again today, which is the market catching up. The rank is a preseason artifact. Never spend a never-resetting claim on it.

Downgraded since yesterday. Schefter reports the Raiders believe Bowers misses only week 1 and returns at the Chargers, so the target vacuum that made Tucker interesting has a return date. Same reasoning applies to your own Michael Mayer — his role probably ends this week.

410 yards and three scores on 56 attempts, and New Orleans are 7.5-point underdogs to Baltimore next. A volume quarterback on a team that trails. Irrelevant while you hold Lawrence, but the right shape if week 7 needs covering — and in this league that patch must be a free agent, never a claim.
